questions.question: Should prompt inputs disappear when using response-only loss?
options: No. They remain context; only their target eligibility changes.
Yes. Masking a prompt token out of the loss also removes it from causal attention.
No, but the logit produced at the final prompt position must be excluded because its input role is prompt.
questions.explanation: Attention visibility and supervised output positions are separate contracts.
optionFeedback: Attention visibility and supervised output positions are separate contracts.
A response-only loss keeps prompt tokens as conditioning inputs. Attention visibility and target eligibility are separate contracts.
Eligibility belongs to the shifted target token, not simply the role of the input position. Inspect the last prompt position’s next-token target.
